body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), there is exactly one continuous function on \([0,\bar\delta]\) that is an almost-everywhere version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).  Hence \(\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P\) is well defined.
body.proof_tex: Existence is part of \(\texttt{def:continuity-model-class}\).  For uniqueness, let \(f\) and \(g\) be two continuous extensions.  Uniqueness of conditional expectations and \(\texttt{ass:conditional-density-law}\) give \(f(a)=g(a)\) for \(\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\)-almost every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\).  By \(\texttt{ass:polynomial-thinning}\), \(\pi_x(a)\geq c_-a^\kappa>0\) for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in(0,\bar\delta]\), so \(f=g\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere on that interval.  If the continuous function \(f-g\) were nonzero at some positive point, it would be bounded away from zero on a nonempty open interval, contradicting almost-everywhere equality.  Thus \(f=g\) on \((0,\bar\delta]\), and continuity at zero yields \(f(0)=g(0)\).
body.justification: The positive-density interior and continuity make the qualitative conditional-regression extension pointwise unique.
body.gap: The continuity-only functional is well defined only after version ambiguity at the threshold is removed.
body.consumer: The lemma fixes the regression value used by the continuity-only causal bridge and observed functional.
